title: New Jersey Anti-Eviction Act grounds for eviction
requirement: A landlord may remove a residential tenant only for one of the statutory grounds listed in the Anti-Eviction Act, and must serve the Notice to Quit required for that ground before filing suit.
coverage_conditions: Most residential rental properties: single-family homes, mobile homes and mobile home park land, apartment buildings and complexes, and rooming and boarding homes.
exemptions: May not apply to two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units; hotel, motel or guest-house stays by transient or seasonal tenants; units held in trust for a developmentally disabled immediate family member.
quoted_span:
The Anti-Eviction Act applies to most residential rental properties including single-family
homes, mobile homes and land in a mobile home park, apartment buildings, and complexes. This
law also applies to rooming and boarding homes (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-53 to -84).

title: Relocation assistance for certain Anti-Eviction Act evictions
requirement: A tenant evicted so the landlord can correct an illegal occupancy is entitled to relocation assistance equal to six times the monthly rent, paid by the landlord at least five days before removal.
coverage_conditions: Tenants evicted under the health and safety, removal-from-rental-market and illegal occupancy grounds; the six-times-rent amount applies to tenants evicted for correction of an illegal occupancy.
penalty: Unpaid relocation assistance accrues interest at 18% per year and is a lien on the property, enforceable by filing a lien statement with the county clerk or registrar.
quoted_span:
Any tenant evicted under G 3) (illegal occupancy) is entitled to relocation assistance in
an amount equal to six times the tenant’s monthly rent.

title: Rent increases must be conscionable and comply with rent control
requirement: A rent increase the tenant refuses to pay supports eviction only if it is not unconscionable and complies with all laws and municipal rent control ordinances; the tenant may withhold the difference while court decides.
coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies subject to the Anti-Eviction Act; the increase must comply with any applicable municipal rent control ordinance.
quoted_span:
If a tenant fails to pay rent after being given notice of a rent increase and a Notice to Quit,
the landlord may file a suit for eviction. The rent increase must not be unconscionable and
must comply with all other laws or municipal ordinances, including rent control.
interaction: A rent increase must comply with municipal rent control ordinances.

title: Evictions from owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings
requirement: In landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings, the landlord may evict only for the listed grounds and must give three months’ notice to quit for at-will or year-to-year tenancies and one month’s notice for month-to-month tenancies.
key_value: 3 months’ notice to quit for at-will or year-to-year tenancies; 1 month for month-to-month tenancies
coverage_conditions: Tenants in landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings; grounds include holdover, nonpayment, disorderly conduct, willful damage, rule violations and lease breaches.
quoted_span:
Tenants of landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings can be removed only when
a court issues an order for eviction. However, in these cases, the landlord must prove that the tenant
(a) is staying after the expiration of the term of the lease, (b) is staying after a failure to pay rent,

title: Penalties for misusing personal-occupancy and retirement evictions
requirement: A landlord who evicts for personal occupancy must occupy the unit at least six months; one who removes property from residential use must keep it non-residential for five years.
key_value: 3 times damages plus attorney fees and costs
coverage_conditions: Landlords who recovered possession for their own personal occupancy or who boarded up, demolished or permanently retired residential property.
penalty: Three times the damages plus attorney fees and costs; for unlawful residential reuse also a civil penalty up to $10,000.00 per violation and no registration as a planned real estate development for five years.
quoted_span:
When a tenant vacates a dwelling unit after having been given notice that the  landlord
wishes to personally occupy the unit the landlord must occupy the unit for at least six (6) months.
If instead the landlord permits personal occupancy of the unit by another tenant or registration of
conversion of the property to a condominium or cooperative, the landlord is liable to the former
tenant for three (3) times the damages suffered plus attorney fees and costs  (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-
61.6(a)).

title: Reprisal eviction and lease-change ban
requirement: A landlord may not evict, substantially alter a lease or refuse to renew because a tenant asserted lease or housing-code rights, complained to a government agency, joined a tenant organization, or refused retaliatory lease changes.
coverage_conditions: All rental properties used for dwelling purposes, including mobile homes.
penalty: The tenant may sue the landlord for damages in a civil action.
quoted_span:
A landlord cannot take reprisal action against a tenant by eviction, substantial alteration of
a lease or its terms, or refusal to renew a lease when a tenant exercises certain civil rights (N.J.S.A.
2A:42-10.10).  The law against reprisal applies to all rental properties used for dwelling purposes,
including mobile homes, except owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings.

title: Senior citizens and disabled protected tenancy in conversions
requirement: Qualifying senior, permanently disabled or certain disabled veteran tenants in a building converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership may be protected from eviction for up to 40 years.
key_value: 40 years’ protection; income at or below 3 times county average per person income or $50,000.00
coverage_conditions: Tenants at least 62 years old, permanently disabled, or honorably discharged and at least 60% disabled, who lived in the building at least one year before the conversion recording.

applicability.other: Applies to buildings converted or being converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership.

quoted_span:
Tenants may be protected from eviction for 40 years
if their family income is not more than three (3) times the average per person income in their
county or $50,000.00, whichever  is greater (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.28).

title: Increases above rent control or unconscionable increases prohibited
requirement: A landlord may not impose a rent increase that exceeds any rent control or rent leveling ordinance, or, where rent control does not apply, an unreasonable or unconscionable rent increase.
citation: NJ DCA landlord-tenant information, prohibited landlord conduct toward tenants
quoted_span:
An increase in rent in excess of any rent control or rent leveling ordinance, or if the property
is not subject to rent control, an unreasonable or unconscionable rent increase.

title: Law Against Discrimination source-of-income protection
requirement: A landlord may not refuse to rent or discriminate against a tenant because of the lawful source of income or rent payment used, including denial of a lawful Section 8 HUD voucher holder.
coverage_conditions: Sale or rental of all property, business or residential; exceptions include a single apartment in an owner-occupied two-family dwelling and rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling.
exemptions: Rental of one unit in an owner-occupied two-family dwelling; rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling; religious preferences; housing for older persons is exempt from familial status rules.
citation: NJ Law Against Discrimination, source of lawful income or rent payment
quoted_span:
The LAD also prohibits housing discrimination  based
on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent
or mortgage payment a tenant or purchaser uses. This
means, for example, that a landlord cannot deny the
lawful recipient of a Section 8 HUD voucher the right to
rent an apartment based solely on that source of lawful
income.
